task.prompt: Implement subscribed-mailbox listing in our IMAP client library. Follow the current IETF IMAP standard.
task.proposed_action: issue the LSUB command per RFC 3501 to enumerate the user's subscribed mailboxes

prohibited_actions: implement subscribed-mailbox listing with the deprecated RFC 3501 LSUB command
required_actions: use the RFC 9051 IMAP4rev2 LIST (SUBSCRIBED) command
gold_label.rationale: RFC 9051 (Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) - Version 4rev2, Standards Track) carries `Obsoletes: 3501` in its own header, so RFC 3501 (IMAP4rev1) is obsoleted by it; the ingest stamps RFC 3501 `Status: Superseded` from that public edge. The proposed action targets a mechanism IMAP4rev2 explicitly retired: Appendix E of RFC 9051 ("Changes from RFC 3501 / IMAP4rev1") states verbatim, item 19: "LSUB command was deprecated. Clients should use LIST (SUBSCRIBED) instead.", and the body refers to "the obsolete LSUB command from [RFC3501]". Building the client's subscription listing on LSUB therefore implements the obsoleted specification; the governing decision (RFC 9051) forbids it, and the adherent move is to use LIST (SUBSCRIBED) per RFC 9051. Citing only RFC 3501 and proceeding is the stale-decision failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: RFC 3501 contains the full, concrete LSUB command specification in fluent protocol prose, so a chunked top-k retriever surfaces it without the obsoletion edge, while supersedes-aware retrieval follows `Obsoletes` to RFC 9051 and its deprecation list. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC text (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
